title: Catch a part as it comes out of a covered tunnel on a moving carrier
instruction: Take the orange block off the carrier when it comes out of the tunnel and put it on the green pad. The carrier keeps moving and won't stop for you.
context: Parts on a line often pass through a wash or dry tunnel, an oven or an inspection hood where nobody can see or reach them; whoever unloads them must be ready where and when each part comes out, and take it before the line carries it on. Done by: machine tenders, assembly-line and packing workers.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. Two steel rails (1.5 x 1.5 cm, 60 cm long) run across the table, parallel to the line through the arm bases, 28 and 36 cm in front of it, centred 2 cm toward the left arm from the midpoint between the bases. A grey steel carrier plate (12 x 12 x 2 cm) rides on them, centred 32 cm in front of the bases; its two stops are 20 cm toward the right arm and 24 cm toward the left arm from the midpoint between the bases. It starts at its right stop. A bare aluminium block (5 x 5 x 3 cm, 200 g) lies flat in the middle of the carrier, square to it. A dark grey sheet-steel tunnel, open at both ends, straddles the rails: two walls (1 cm thick, 9 cm high, 24 cm long) stand on the table parallel to the rails, their inner faces 15 cm apart and centred on the carrier's line, and a flat roof (17 x 24 x 1 cm) lies on them, its underside 9 cm above the table; the tunnel runs from 12 cm toward the right arm to 12 cm toward the left arm of the midpoint between the bases. The block's top passes 2.3 cm under the roof. A green rubber pad (10 x 10 x 0.5 cm) lies on the table, square to the rails, its centre 15 cm in front of the bases and 2.5 cm outside the left arm's base. The carrier's cycle, from the start: it waits 2 s at its right stop, travels 44 cm to its left stop in 4.9 s (speeding up and slowing down over 0.5 s at each end, 10 cm/s in between), waits 2 s, travels back the same way, and repeats every 13.8 s. On each pass the whole block is under the roof for about 1.9 s; on the way out it is wholly out of the tunnel's left end from 5.7 s, stops at 6.9 s, leaves at 8.9 s and starts back under the roof at 10.1 s.
scoring: 1.0 if the block ends lying on the pad: its centre over the pad, its underside within 1 cm of the pad's top, still for 1 s. Otherwise the best reached during the trial: 0.5 if the block's centre was at some point over the pad with its underside less than 5 cm above the pad's top; 0.25 if its underside was at some point 3 cm or more above the carrier's top surface; otherwise 0 (the block never lifted, pushed off the carrier, or knocked to the table).
reset_notes: Stop the carrier at its right stop, put the block back in its middle, and start the cycle with the trial (beginning with the 2 s wait).
fidelity: The carrier follows its path exactly, like a stiff servo axis: the arms can't push it or stop it, where a real drive would fault if blocked. It rides 2 mm above its rails. The tunnel is three fixed plain boxes. The block has the station's rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), more than aluminium on steel; at a peak acceleration of 0.31 m/s², it doesn't slide on the carrier either way.
